title: PSA: Vibecoding does not mean you get a pass on quality standards
author: aj_marshall
selftext:
So look gang

I like using AI. I am not a SWE, but I've been writing code for the better part of a decade and doing engineering for about twice that length. There has always been no shortage of tools people have been willing to try and use to expedite their ability to make a product. (as an aside, I recall a time back when "digital artists" were not looked upon as "real artists" because they got to use these fancy things called *layers*!)

However, using a tool of any kind does not mean consumers of your product need to give you *any* kind of slack in the quality of what you're shipping.

Do your art assets look bad? Then make new ones!

Does your audio sound generic and bland? Produce some more!

Do your menus keep bugging out? Fix them!

Does your game crash if the player goes off the intended path? Box that shit in!

You can and should use AI to make your dreams come to life- but if people can obviously tell your product was "made with AI", that's usually a tell that your product is lacking polish they were otherwise expecting.

So, my fellow devs- AI can do a lot for you, but it can't tell you when something is good enough. You have to hold the standard, and you need to stop publishing the moment you get an MVP. 

Enjoy vibing!

comments.author: No_Individual_6528
comments.body: I think in this world of AI games.  The hardest problem is the last 10% for sure. And maybe a great game mechanic can save a game. But a lot of games won't be that and therefore feel like slop.

comments.author: johnesco
comments.body: Enjoy vibing, Stop "one-shotting". And playtest playtest playtest, then teach your ai to playtest it and pair up.

replies.author: Coolbanh
replies.body: Yeah most of those ai influencers/youtubers tend to focus on 1 shotting a working game. There's really a lot that goes into that and making a game has never been easier.

replies.author: johnesco
replies.body:
I've made trivial games before in JS. Hangman, using the DOM or maybe Canvas tag. As soon as I started vibe coding I suddenly had a working prototype with the ability to tweak at will in plain English. I'm sure my progress as a "product" pales to what I see other people doing, but that's not so much the point. My game is my FIRST game of this size. First program of this size. Learning about CI/CD, the different ways to branch or version. Using some tools one would use in groups, to keep a "tell me in plain English what you did because, no I can't read the code". Incidentally, if you can't read your own code yet, there are areas and complexities that will trip you up badly, but they are learnable. I'm just making a webgame and don't feel it's a threat to people if I have some unoptimized spaghetti code. It works and I'm not copying or spitting out a game. I'm designing it as I go. Enjoying it, recording it for posterity. I'm doing it for me, but, I \*am\* one of the top racing games among the AI gen games on Itch.

I want to spend time sharing these stories with others who are discovering the same, but the toxicity makes me just want to go heads down and vibe til I'll I'm bored of it (which could be in 2 weeks, or 2 years or 2 decades.)

comments.author: Due_Interest_178
comments.body: If vibe coders posted a lot more quality games versus "here's my one shot spiderman/whatever game" then I think it'd be a lot more accepted

replies.author: AN1mbleNavigator
replies.body: Agreed, problem I think right now is people are posting their 24 hour made game while I’m 8 months into development and not ready to show off the game still. The models have been only really getting good at game dev this year so I think it’s just in due time.

replies.author: drallcom3
replies.body:
> If vibe coders posted a lot more quality games

You'd probably also have 99% less AI "games". 50% of the stuff posted here is not even a game. Just a tech demo. At best. Often just a trailer.

comments.author: drallcom3
comments.body: Does it really matter? The audience will silently judge by either playing or not playing your game.

comments.author: khyrichan
comments.body:
Personally, the part I struggle with the most in my MMORPG is the UI. Making it intuitive, beautiful, and functional takes an insane amount of time, and I'm constantly revisiting it to improve things. I never expected the UI to take up so much of my development time.

It's amazing how much we learn every day. When I look back at what I was doing with Claude six months ago, I realize how bad I actually was, even though I thought I was already doing incredible things back then. And tomorrow, I'll probably look at how I use AI today and all my current fixes and think the exact same thing. 😅

replies.author: Arya_the_Gamer
replies.body: For UI, I would suggest looking at some good examples and try to understand what makes them so good.

replies.author: khyrichan
replies.body: Yes, and I'll try using Claude Design as well.

comments.author: Historical_architect
comments.body: I don’t think I’d ever get to a point where I’d even invest in something that is vibecoded not because the idea is bad or poorly executed but because I wouldn’t trust the maker to continually do the work to support it through bugs, os/security updates, etc. software takes a team to support it. A dude with Claude doesn’t have that kind of infrastructure

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

comments.author: Sylvester11062
comments.body: Also those of us that see AI slop need to call it out when we see it. Theres a legitimate witch-hunt for anything related to AI these days and people posting and boasting about their “games” that look like one shot prompts are actively making things worse.

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body: Yep. If I see slop around here, I call it slop. If your project is being called slop in one of the more friendly AI development subs, it's probably slop and you need to fix that.

comments.author: Gorden121
comments.body:
That's not just advice for game dev but generally.  
AI does not either consumers or coworkers give you any more slack than doing it in any other way.  
Of you can't code that's fine, you can still care about the architecture and get a general feel of how things *should* run and look.  
You should make sure you at least have a general understanding of what happens when and ofc make sure the output is working properly e.g. test it.

comments.author: Decent_Departure9874
comments.body: It is all about the testing. Ai can generatie shitload of code/game content, but the goal is that the game should be fun. You need a human for that (assuming you try to entertain humans). You can built some auto game testing, but a human MUST be in the loop. This  is why vibe coding games is for now still time consuming (if you do it right)
